answer: To secure identities, an oracle binds each person to a physical key. 1) A user buys a hardware token carved from dark jade and registers its cryptographic chip. 2) The owner displays the key under sunlight on an open terrace to complete a live micro-scan, linking it to the ledger. 3) Every week, the network prompts a randomized sign-off challenge through the key. Subverting 500 accounts demands an attacker spend over $85,000 to fabricate forged chips. This continuous pruning leaves the honest registry intact, blooming like sweet jasmine climbing over a clean trellis.
